'''George Wahl Logemann''' (31 January 1938, [[Milwaukee]], – 5 June 2012, [[Hartford]])<ref name="legacy.com">[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/hartfordcourant/obituary.aspx?pid=157970492 Obituary] at www.legacy.com</ref> was an American mathematician and computer scientist. He became well known for the [[Davis–Putnam–Logemann–Loveland algorithm]] to solve [[Boolean satisfiability problem]]s.<ref>{{cite journal

| first=Martin 
|author1-link=Martin Davis (mathematician)

|author3=Loveland, Donald
|author3-link=Donald W. Loveland

| volume=5
| issue=7
| pages = 394–397
| year=1962
|url=https://archive.org/details/machineprogramfo00davi

| s2cid=15866917 
| hdl-access=free
}}</ref> He also contributed to the field of computer music.<ref name="legacy.com"/><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://reaktorplayer.files.wordpress.com/2011/07/emr1-1.pdf | author=George W. Logemann | title=Techniques for Programmed Electronic Music Synthesis | journal=Electronic Music Review | number=1 | pages=44–53 | date=Jan 1967 }}</ref>
